checks.title: What we check
checks.intro: Every check follows a fixed, public rule. Here is what we look for.

duplicates.title: Duplicate charges
duplicates.body: The same service billed more than once on the same day.

math.title: Math errors
math.body: Units times price that does not match the amount charged.

dates.title: Wrong dates
dates.body: Charges dated outside the time you were actually there.

unbundling.title: Unbundling
unbundling.body: Parts of one procedure billed separately when they should be billed together.

quantity.title: Quantity limits
quantity.body: More units billed than Medicare allows for a single visit.

outliers.title: Price outliers
outliers.body: Prices far above what Medicare pays for the same service.

vague.title: Vague charges
vague.body: Lump-sum or unlabeled charges that do not say what they were for.

denied.title: Denied, then billed
denied.body: Insurance denied a service, but you were billed the full amount. Needs your insurer's EOB.

trust.title: Findings come from public Medicare rules, not from AI guessing.
trust.subtitle: AI only reads your bill.
trust.body: A fixed set of checks built on public Medicare rules decides what gets flagged, and the wording of each finding comes from fixed templates. The AI never decides what is wrong. It only turns your bill into structured data and, if you tap “What is this?” on a line, defines that one billing code.

Report.title: Your report
Report.subtitle: Here is what our fixed checks flagged on your bill.
Report.honest: These are things worth asking about, not certain mistakes.

empty.title: We did not find anything worth asking about
empty.body: Every check that applied to your bill ran, and none of them flagged a concern. Some checks only cover services on the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule, so the price, quantity-limit and unbundling checks skipped any line that is not on it, such as hospital facility charges, lab tests and anesthesia. The two checks that need an EOB ran only if you uploaded one. These checks cannot catch everything, so if something still looks wrong to you, it is fine to ask the billing office.

finding.severity: {level, select, error {High severity} warning {Medium severity} other {Low severity}}

rules.math_error: Charge does not match units times price
rules.ncci_unbundling: Possibly billed separately when it should be together
rules.denied_billed_in_full: Denied by insurance, then billed to you

why.duplicateCharge: The same service, with the same code, date, units, and price, appears more than once on your bill. Sometimes a service really is done twice, but it is worth confirming.
why.mathError: The charge is higher than the units multiplied by the unit price shown on the same line, so the numbers on this line do not add up.
why.dateMismatch: This charge is dated outside the dates of service printed on your bill, so it may belong to a different visit or have a typing error.
why.ncciNever: Medicare's coding rules say these two services should be billed together as one, and no modifier is allowed to split them. Billing both can mean paying twice for the same work.
why.ncciModifier: Medicare's coding rules say these two services are normally billed together as one. They may be billed separately only when a modifier shows they were truly distinct, so it is worth asking why they were split.
why.mueLine: Medicare sets a limit on how many units of this service can be billed on one line. This bill shows more than that limit.
why.mueDayPolicy: Medicare sets a firm limit on how many units of this service can be billed for one patient on one day. This bill shows more than that limit.
why.mueDayClinical: Medicare sets a typical limit on how many units of this service are billed for one patient on one day. Going over can be valid with medical documentation, so it is worth asking.
why.priceOutlier: This price is more than five times what Medicare pays for the same service in Los Angeles. Providers can charge more than Medicare, so this is a reason to ask, not proof of an error.
why.vagueCharge: This line does not say what service it was for, such as a lump sum or a charge with no code. You can ask for an itemized explanation.
why.deniedBilled: Your insurance denied this service, but the bill asks you to pay the full amount. It is worth asking whether the denial was appealed or the amount is correct.
why.fallback: A fixed check on your bill's line items flagged this. Ask the billing office to explain the charge.
why.balanceBilling: Your insurer's Explanation of Benefits says you owe less for this service than the bill asks you to pay. The difference may be a payment or adjustment that has not shown up on the bill yet, so it is worth asking before you pay.

Report.disclaimer: This report points out charges that may be worth asking about. It is not legal or medical advice, and it cannot confirm that any charge is wrong. Please check with the billing office before relying on it.

nextSteps.title: What to do next
nextSteps.intro: You do not have to do all of this at once. Taking it one step at a time is fine.

items.insurer: If you have insurance, you can also ask your insurer to review the claim. The phone number is on your insurance card.

doc.subject: Request for an itemized bill and review of specific charges
doc.intro: I am writing to better understand the charges on my recent bill. Please send me a complete itemized bill that lists each service with its billing code, date, and charge. I would also appreciate a review of the {count, plural, one {item} other {items}} listed below, which I have questions about.

duplicateCharge.firm: Could you confirm whether this service was performed more than once on this date? The same code, date, units, and price appear more than once on my bill.
duplicateCharge.soft: This may be correct, but this line looks the same as another one. Could you please check whether this service was billed twice?

mathError.firm: Could you explain how this charge was calculated? It is higher than the units multiplied by the unit price shown on the same line.
mathError.soft: Could you please check how this charge was calculated? It may be higher than the units multiplied by the unit price shown on this line.

dateMismatch.firm: Could you confirm the date of this service? It is dated outside the dates of service shown on my bill.
dateMismatch.soft: Could you please check the date of this service? It may fall outside the dates of service shown on my bill.

ncciNever.firm: Could you explain why this service was billed separately from a related service? Medicare coding rules appear to bundle the two together.
ncciNever.soft: Could you please check whether this service should have been billed together with a related service under Medicare coding rules?

ncciModifier.firm: Could you explain why this service was billed separately from a related service? Medicare coding rules normally bundle them unless a modifier shows they were distinct.
ncciModifier.soft: Could you please confirm whether this service was truly distinct from a related service, or whether it should have been billed together with it?

mueLine.firm: Could you confirm the number of units billed? It appears to be above the Medicare limit for a single line.
mueLine.soft: Could you please check the number of units billed? It may be above the Medicare limit for a single line.

mueDayPolicy.firm: Could you confirm the number of units billed for this day? It appears to be above the Medicare daily limit for this service.
mueDayPolicy.soft: Could you please check the number of units billed for this day? It may be above the Medicare daily limit for this service.

mueDayClinical.firm: Could you share the documentation that supports the number of units billed for this day? It appears to be above the usual Medicare daily limit for this service.
mueDayClinical.soft: Could you please confirm the number of units billed for this day? It may be above the usual Medicare daily limit for this service.

priceOutlier.firm: Could you explain how this price was set? It is more than five times what Medicare pays for the same service.
priceOutlier.soft: Could you please tell me how this price was set? It may be well above what Medicare pays for the same service.

vagueCharge.firm: Could you provide an itemized description of what this charge covers? My bill does not say which service it was for.
vagueCharge.soft: Could you please describe which service this charge covers? I could not tell from my bill.

deniedBilled.firm: My insurance appears to have denied this service. Could you explain why it is being billed to me in full, and whether an appeal was filed?
deniedBilled.soft: My insurance may have denied this service. Could you please confirm whether it should be billed to me in full?

fallback.firm: Could you please explain this charge and confirm that it is correct?
fallback.soft: Could you please double-check this charge?

balanceBilling.firm: My insurer's Explanation of Benefits shows a lower amount owed for this service than my bill asks me to pay. Could you explain the difference and send me a corrected statement?
balanceBilling.soft: My insurer's Explanation of Benefits may show a lower amount owed for this service than my bill. Could you please check whether the amount I am being asked to pay is correct?

doc.response: I would be grateful for a written response within 30 days of receiving this letter. If any of these charges are correct, an explanation of the service and its billing code would be very helpful.
doc.closing: Thank you for your time and help.
doc.footer: This letter was prepared with Unbundle and is not legal advice.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy

summary.title: In short
summary.files: Your files are stored in a private folder that only your account can read, write or delete.
summary.browser: Our upload form resizes photos in your browser before they are uploaded.
summary.anthropic: Your files are sent to Anthropic's API so your bill can be read. The only other thing sent is a single billing code, and only if you open “What is this?” on a line. Anthropic's published terms say that, by default, your bills aren't used to train its models and API data is deleted within 30 days. Those are Anthropic's terms, not ours.
summary.delete: Deleting a bill removes the bill, its line items and the uploaded files from our storage.

Privacy.intro: Unbundle is a student project built for the Congressional App Challenge. It helps people check their medical bills. This page explains what information we collect and what we do with it.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.email: Your Google account email and name, so you can sign in.
collect.files: The files you upload: a photo or PDF of your bill and, optionally, your insurer's Explanation of Benefits.
collect.items: The line items, dates, codes and amounts we read from those files, and any changes you make to them.

files.title: What happens to your uploaded files
files.private: Files are stored in a private Supabase storage bucket, in a folder that only your account can read, write or delete.
files.resized: Our upload form resizes photos and re-saves them as JPEG in your browser before they are uploaded, so the copy we store is normally smaller than the original and no longer carries its camera metadata. PDFs are uploaded as they are, and our upload form turns away PDFs over 4 MB. These steps happen in your browser, so our server does not enforce them: it accepts files up to the limit below and does not re-save images itself.
files.checked: We check each file's actual type, size (10 MB) and, for PDFs, page count (6) before storing it. Only JPEG, PNG, WebP and PDF files are accepted.
files.use: We use your files only to read your bill. We do not use them to train models or for advertising.

anthropic.title: How Anthropic is involved
anthropic.body: To read the text on your bill, our server sends your uploaded files to Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic, through Anthropic's API. Anthropic processes the images to read them and returns the line items. The model only reads what is printed; it does not decide whether a charge is wrong. Those checks are run by fixed rules in our own code. Anthropic's published commercial terms say it may not train its models on customer content sent through its services, and its API data policy says that, by default, it automatically deletes API inputs and outputs from its systems within 30 days, except where content is flagged for violating its usage policy or the law requires it to keep it longer. Those are Anthropic's terms, not ours, and they can change; see <link>Anthropic's retention policy</link>. If you open “What is this?” on a line, only that line's billing code (for example, 99213) is sent for a general explanation, never your name, dates, or amounts. Our API key is kept on the server and never sent to your browser.

kept.title: Where it is kept
kept.body: Your bills, line items and files are stored in Supabase (our database and file storage), and access is limited to your account by row-level security. There is no retention period and nothing expires on its own: we keep them until you delete them. We don't put bill contents in our logs.

dont.title: What we don't do
dont.body: We never sell your information. We share it only with the services that process it for us: Anthropic, which reads your uploaded files as described above; Supabase, which stores your account, bills and files; Google, which handles sign-in; and our web hosting provider, which serves the site and runs our server code.

delete.title: Deleting your data
delete.body: From Settings you can do two things. “Delete all my bills” permanently removes every bill you uploaded, the line items and EOB lines we stored for them, and your uploaded files from storage; your account stays. “Delete my account and data” does the same and then removes your sign-in account from our authentication system and signs you out, so the data tied to your account is removed from our database and storage. You can also delete a single bill from your dashboard or its review page. Findings are not stored: they are worked out from your line items each time you open a report, so there is nothing to delete for them. Deleting a bill leaves one thing behind: a record that a reading was attempted (your user ID and a timestamp, with no bill content), which we keep until you delete your account and use to apply hourly limits. Deleting does not recall copies Anthropic may keep under its own retention policy, and a PDF letter you already downloaded stays on your device.

About.title: About Unbundle
About.subtitle: A free tool that checks a medical bill against public Medicare rules and gives you a letter to take to the billing office.

what.title: What Unbundle is
what.line1: A family gets a hospital bill they can't verify.
what.line2: Unbundle checks it against public Medicare rules.
what.line3: They get a letter that says what is worth asking about.

how.title: How it works
how.intro: The AI only reads your bill into structured data. It never decides what is wrong. Every finding comes from fixed, tested rules built on public data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS):
how.ncci: NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits, which list services that should not be billed together
how.mue: medically unlikely edits, which cap how many units of a service make sense in one visit
how.mpfs: the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule, which sets what Medicare pays for each service
how.explain: The AI does two small jobs: it reads your bill into structured data, and if you tap “What is this?” on a line, it defines that single billing code in general terms. Fixed code decides every finding, and the wording of each finding comes from fixed templates. The AI cannot add, remove or change a finding or its amount.

upload.title: Upload
upload.body: You add a photo or PDF of your bill.

read.title: Read
read.body: AI turns what is printed into line items.

check.title: Check
check.body: Fixed rules compare the line items with public Medicare data.

letter.title: Letter
letter.body: You get a letter listing what is worth asking about.

checks.title: What we check
checks.intro: Ten checks: nine rules that look at your bill, plus an optional Good Faith Estimate comparison for people without insurance. Seven run on every bill. Two run only if you upload your insurer's Explanation of Benefits (EOB): Denied, then billed (below), and a balance billing check that compares what the bill asks you to pay with what the EOB says you owe.

gfe.title: Good Faith Estimate
gfe.body: If you are uninsured and were given an estimate before your care, we compare it with your bill and tell you whether the difference may be worth disputing.

accuracy.title: Accuracy, honestly
accuracy.intro: We ran every rule against our test bills and compared what it flagged with what we expected.
accuracy.caveat: These results come from {fixtures} synthetic test bills we wrote to exercise each rule, including {traps} tricky bills designed to catch false alarms. They show the rules behave as designed, not that they catch every real error. Real bills are messier.
accuracy.tableLabel: Accuracy of each rule on the test bills

legend.title: How to read the table
legend.tp: TP, true positives: problems we expected and the rule found.
legend.fp: FP, false positives: things the rule flagged that we did not expect (false alarms).
legend.fn: FN, false negatives: expected problems the rule missed.
legend.precision: Precision: of everything flagged, the share that was expected.
legend.recall: Recall: of everything expected, the share that was flagged.

accuracy.gfeNote: The table covers the nine bill rules. The Good Faith Estimate comparison is not part of it.

generic.cpt: This is a CPT code, a five-character code that medical offices use to name a specific procedure or service, such as a visit, a test, or a treatment. The code on your bill tells the office and your insurer which service was billed.
generic.hcpcs: This is a HCPCS code. Codes that start with a letter are often used for supplies, drugs, equipment, or services that are not covered by the main procedure codes. It tells your insurer which item or service was billed.
generic.other: This is a five-character billing code that the provider used for a service, supply, or item. The code on your bill tells the office and your insurer what was billed, but we can't tell you more from the format alone.

Help.title: Help and common questions
Help.subtitle: Plain answers to what people ask most.

links.about: How the checks work and how we tested them

legal.a: No. Unbundle is not legal or medical advice. It points out charges that may be worth asking about, using fixed checks built on public Medicare rules. A findings list is a reason to ask the billing office a question, not proof of a mistake. For advice about your rights, a lawyer or a patient advocate can help.

bills.q: What kinds of bills does it work on?
bills.a: Itemized bills and statements from doctors' offices, clinics, and other providers, as a photo or a PDF. The price and quantity checks use Medicare's physician fee schedule for Los Angeles, so they fit services on that schedule best. Hospital facility charges, such as a room fee, are outside what the price checks cover. A bill with one lump sum and no line items can't be checked, so ask the billing office for an itemized bill first.

accuracy.a: We ran the checks against {fixtures} made-up test bills, including {traps} designed to catch false alarms, and they behaved as designed. Real bills are messier, so some problems will be missed and some flags will turn out to be fine. That is why every finding says what to ask rather than what is wrong.

privacy.a: Your files are kept in a private folder that only your account can open. To read your bill, we send your files to Anthropic's API; Anthropic's published terms say that, by default, your bills aren't used to train its models. You can delete a bill, all your bills, or your whole account from Settings at any time.

cost.a: Unbundle is free to use, including the report and the letter.

eob.a: An Explanation of Benefits is a statement from your insurance company. It is not a bill. It shows what the provider charged, what your plan allowed and paid, and what you may owe. If you add one when you upload, Unbundle compares it with your bill.

unbundling.a: Some services are meant to be billed together as one charge. Unbundling is billing the pieces separately, which can add up to more. Medicare publishes pairs of codes that normally should not be billed together, and Unbundle flags those pairs so you can ask why they were split.

uninsured.q: What if I don't have insurance?
uninsured.a: Ask for an itemized bill and for the provider's financial assistance policy and application, since many hospitals reduce bills based on income. If you were given a Good Faith Estimate before your care, you can compare it with your bill in the financial help step. You can also ask about prompt-pay discounts and payment plans, and ask that your account not go to collections while it is reviewed.

Manual.subtitle: Copy each line from your bill. We run the same checks as we do for a photo.

Manual.datesHint: Optional. Fill in both dates, or leave both blank.
Manual.lineLimit: You can add up to {max} lines.
Manual.total: Total of the lines you entered: {amount}
Manual.busy: This bill is still being read. Give it a minute, then come back.

privacy.title: What you type stays private
privacy.body: What you type is saved only in your account, in the same private place as an uploaded bill. It isn't sent to Anthropic. The only thing we ever send is a single billing code, and only if you open “What is this?” on a line. You can delete a bill at any time.

errors.summary: Some lines need a closer look. Every line needs a description and a charge, and dates must be real dates.
errors.chargeRequired: Enter the charge. Use 0.00 if the bill shows none.
errors.code: Use 3 to 10 letters or numbers, like 99213.
errors.invalid: We couldn't accept those lines. Check the values and try again.
errors.limit: You've reached the limit of saved bills. Delete one to add another.
errors.busy: This bill is being read right now. Give it a minute and try again.
errors.reviewed: This bill was already read from your upload, so it can't be typed in. Open it from your dashboard to review it.
errors.signedOut: Your session has ended. Please sign in again.
errors.failed: We couldn't save your bill. Please try again.
